title: Debate Collapses to Monologue: Quantifying How Homogeneity Kills Scalable-Oversight Debate

original_idea.body:
# Debate Collapses to Monologue: Quantifying How Homogeneity Kills Scalable-Oversight Debate

**Problem:** Debate-based scalable oversight only works when debaters have divergent knowledge; homogeneous debaters reduce debate to a single agent.

**Direction:** Run a two-debater + judge setup on factual claims. Vary debater 'distance' (same model two roles vs different lineages) and measure judge accuracy, using output-homogeneity as the independent variable.

**Why it matters:** Debate is a leading scalable-oversight bet; if deployed models are homogeneous, debate may give a false sense of oversight.

**Relevant context:** 'Knowledge Divergence and the Value of Debate' (arXiv 2603.05293); Artificial Hivemind.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Tests a leading scalable-oversight bet labs deprioritize stress-testing; public models, no infra.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over open models in a debate loop, one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Knowledge-divergence-and-debate is studied; using output-homogeneity as the axis empirically may be open.
